questions.questionTextEn: The _________ is too high for it to be considered _________.
optionsEn: fair / fare
faer / fair
fare / fare
fare / fair
questions.explanationEn: In English usage, 'fare' refers to the price charged for a journey or service, while 'fair' means reasonable or just. Therefore, 'The fare is too high for it to be considered fair' is the only grammatically and semantically correct option.

questions.questionTextEn:
Let r be a root of the equation xଶ+ 2x+ 6 = 0.
Then the value of the expression (r+ 2)(r+ 3)(r+ 4)(r+ 5) is
questions.explanationEn: Since r^2 + 2r + 6 = 0, completing the square gives (r + 1)^2 = -5. Letting u = r + 1, we have (r+2)(r+5) = (u+1)(u+4) = u^2 + 5u + 4 = 5u - 1 and (r+3)(r+4) = (u+2)(u+3) = u^2 + 5u + 6 = 5u + 1, so their product is (5u - 1)(5u + 1) = 25u^2 - 1 = 25(-5) - 1 = -126.

questions.questionTextEn:
Given below are four statements.
Statement 1: All students are inquisitive.
Statement 2: Some students are inquisitive.
Statement 3: No student is inquisitive.
Statement 4: Some students are not inquisitive.
From the given four statements, find the two statements that CANNOT BE
TRUE simultaneously, assuming that there is at least one student in the class.
optionsEn: Statement 1 and Statement 3
Statement 1 and Statement 2
Statement 2 and Statement 4
Statement 3 and Statement 4
questions.explanationEn: Assuming at least one student exists in the class, Statement 1 ('All students are inquisitive') and Statement 3 ('No student is inquisitive') are logical contraries. They cannot both be true at the same time.

questions.questionTextEn:
Some people believe that “what gets measured, improves”. Some others believe
that “what gets measured, gets gamed”. One possible reason for the difference in
the beliefs is the work culture in organizations. In organizations with good work
culture, metrics help improve outcomes. However, the same metrics are
counterproductive in organizations with poor work culture.
Which one of the following is the CORRECT logical inference based on the
information in the above passage?
optionsEn: Metrics are useful in organizations with poor work culture
Metrics are useful in organizations with good work culture
Metrics are always counterproductive in organizations with good work culture
Metrics are never useful in organizations with good work culture
questions.explanationEn: The passage explicitly states that in organizations with good work culture, metrics help improve outcomes, while in those with poor work culture they are counterproductive. Thus, Option (B) follows directly from the passage.

questions.questionTextEn:
In a recently conducted national entrance test, boys constituted 65% of those who
appeared for the test. Girls constituted the remaining candidates and they
accounted for 60% of the qualified candidates.
Which one of the following is the correct logical inference based on the
information provided in the above passage?
optionsEn: Equal number of boys and girls qualified
Equal number of boys and girls appeared for the test
The number of boys who appeared for the test is less than the number of girls who appeared
The number of boys who qualified the test is less than the number of girls who qualified
questions.explanationEn: Out of the total qualified candidates, girls accounted for 60%, which implies boys accounted for the remaining 40%. Since 40% < 60%, the number of boys who qualified is strictly less than the number of girls who qualified.

questions.questionTextEn:
A box contains five balls of same size and shape. Three of them are green
coloured balls and two of them are orange coloured balls. Balls are drawn from
the box one at a time. If a green ball is drawn, it is not replaced. If an orange ball
is drawn, it is replaced with another orange ball.
First ball is drawn. What is the probability of getting an orange ball in the next
draw?
questions.explanationEn: Initially there are 3 green and 2 orange balls. By the law of total probability, P(2nd is orange) = P(1st is green)*P(2nd is orange | 1st green) + P(1st is orange)*P(2nd is orange | 1st orange) = (3/5)*(2/4) + (2/5)*(2/5) = 3/10 + 4/25 = 23/50.

questions.questionTextEn:
The corners and mid-points of the sides of a triangle are named using the distinct
letters P, Q, R, S, T and U, but not necessarily in the same order. Consider the
following statements:
• The line joining P and R is parallel to the line joining Q and S.
• P is placed on the side opposite to the corner T.
• S and U cannot be placed on the same side.
Which one of the following statements is correct based on the above
information?
optionsEn: P cannot be placed at a corner
S cannot be placed at a corner
U cannot be placed at a mid-point
R cannot be placed at a corner
questions.explanationEn: By the midpoint theorem, PR being parallel to QS implies one pair consists of the midpoints of two sides and the other consists of the corners of the third side. Since P lies on the side opposite corner T and S and U cannot share a side, P and R must be the corners on that opposite side while Q and S are the midpoints of the other two sides, so S cannot be placed at a corner.

What is the least number of additional straight ropes needed to create the
desired plots? A single rope can pass through three poles that are aligned in a
straight line.
questions.explanationEn: To partition the grid into four plots of similar shape with ropes R1 and R2 fixed, each straight rope can connect three collinear poles. Adding 3 more straight ropes completes the required four similar regions (refer to the official grid diagram).

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
optionsEn: The (1) LALR parser for a grammar G cannot have reduce-reduce conflict if the (1) LR parser for G does not have reduce-reduce conflict.
Symbol table is accessed only during the lexical analysis phase.
Data flow analysis is necessary for run-time memory management.
(1) LR parsing is sufficient for deterministic context-free languages.
questions.explanationEn: Every deterministic context-free language (DCFL) has an LR(1) grammar, so LR(1) parsing is sufficient to parse all DCFLs. The other statements are false: LALR(1) can introduce reduce-reduce conflicts absent in LR(1), symbol tables are used across semantic/code-gen phases too, and data flow analysis is for compile-time optimization.

questions.questionTextEn: In a relational data model, which one of the following statements is TRUE?
optionsEn: A relation with only two attributes is always in BCNF.
If all attributes of a relation are prime attributes, then the relation is in BCNF.
Every relation has at least one non-prime attribute.
BCNF decompositions preserve functional dependencies.
questions.explanationEn: In a binary relation R(A, B), the only possible non-trivial functional dependencies are A -> B or B -> A. In either case, the left-hand side is a superkey of R, guaranteeing that every 2-attribute relation is always in BCNF.

questions.explanationEn: With simple uniform hashing, each key—whether hashed by h1 (odd) or h2 (even)—is mapped uniformly and independently to any of the m slots with probability 1/m. By linearity of expectation over n keys, the expected number of keys in any slot is n/m.

questions.questionTextEn:
Which one of the following facilitates transfer of bulk data from hard disk to main
memory with the highest throughput?
optionsEn: DMA based I/O transfer
Interrupt driven I/O transfer
Polling based I/O transfer
Programmed I/O transfer
questions.explanationEn: Direct Memory Access (DMA) allows the disk controller to transfer blocks of data directly to main memory without CPU intervention for each word. This minimizes CPU overhead and yields the highest data transfer throughput compared to polling, programmed I/O, or interrupt-driven I/O.

Let R1 and R2 be two 4-bit registers that store numbers in 2’s complement form.
For the operation R1+R2, which one of the following values of R1 and R2 gives an
arithmetic overflow?
questions.explanationEn: In 4-bit 2's complement representation, the valid range is [-8, +7]. For R1 = 1100 (-4) and R2 = 1010 (-6), their sum is -10, which falls outside [-8, +7] and causes arithmetic underflow/overflow (while the other pairs yield -7, +7, and -8, all within range).

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider an enterprise network with two Ethernet segments, a web server and a
firewall, connected via three routers as shown below.
What is the number of subnets inside the enterprise network?
questions.explanationEn: Counting the isolated broadcast domains (each Ethernet segment, point-to-point router-to-router link, and server/firewall link separated by router interfaces) in the enterprise topology gives 6 distinct subnets (refer to the official network diagram).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: Every subset of a recursively enumerable language is recursive.
If a language L and its complement L are both recursively enumerable, then L must be recursive.
Complement of a context-free language must be recursive.
If 1L and 2L are regular, then 1 2 L L ∩ must be deterministic context-free.
questions.explanationEn: If both L and its complement are recursively enumerable, L is decidable/recursive (B). Context-free languages are recursive and recursive languages are closed under complement, so the complement of a CFL is recursive (C). Regular languages are closed under intersection and every regular language is deterministic context-free (D).

questions.questionTextEn:
Let WB and WT be two set associative cache organizations that use LRU algorithm
for cache block replacement. WB is a write back cache and WT is a write through
cache. Which of the following statements is/are FALSE?
optionsEn: Each cache block in WB and WT has a dirty bit.
Every write hit in WB leads to a data transfer from cache to main memory.
Eviction of a block from WT will not lead to data transfer from cache to main memory.
A read miss in WB will never lead to eviction of a dirty block from WB.
questions.explanationEn: A write-through (WT) cache immediately propagates writes to memory and does not need a dirty bit (so A is false). In a write-back (WB) cache, write hits only update the cache block and set the dirty bit without writing to memory (B is false), and a read miss can evict a dirty block (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements is/are TRUE with respect to deadlocks?
optionsEn: Circular wait is a necessary condition for the formation of deadlock.
In a system where each resource has more than one instance, a cycle in its wait-for graph indicates the presence of a deadlock.
If the current allocation of resources to processes leads the system to unsafe state, then deadlock will necessarily occur.
In the resource-allocation graph of a system, if every edge is an assignment edge, then the system is not in deadlock state.
questions.explanationEn: Circular wait is one of the four necessary Coffman conditions for deadlock (A). If every edge in a resource-allocation graph is an assignment edge (no request edges), no process is waiting on any resource, so no deadlock exists (D). With multi-instance resources a cycle is necessary but not sufficient (B false), and an unsafe state does not guarantee deadlock (C false).

questions.questionTextEn:
Suppose a binary search tree with 1000 distinct elements is also a complete binary
tree. The tree is stored using the array representation of binary heap trees. Assuming
that the array indices start with 0, the 3rd largest element of the tree is stored at
index_____________.
questions.explanationEn: In a 0-indexed complete BST with 1000 nodes, levels 0–8 hold 511 nodes (indices 0–510) and level 9 holds 489 nodes (indices 511–999, whose last parent is index 499). Hence the rightmost nodes at level 8 are leaves at indices 500–510, making index 510 the largest element, its parent 254 the 2nd largest, and the left child of 254 (index 509) the 3rd largest.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a simple undirected graph of 10 vertices. If the graph is disconnected, then
the maximum number of edges it can have is ____________.
questions.explanationEn: To maximize edges in a disconnected simple undirected graph on n = 10 vertices, partition the vertices into a clique of size n - 1 = 9 and an isolated vertex of size 1. This yields C(9, 2) = 9*8/2 = 36 edges.

questions.questionTextEn: The number of arrangements of six identical balls in three identical bins is______.
questions.explanationEn: Arranging 6 identical balls into 3 identical bins (where bins may be empty) corresponds to the integer partitions of 6 into at most 3 parts. The partitions are (6), (5,1), (4,2), (4,1,1), (3,3), (3,2,1), and (2,2,2), giving 7 arrangements.

questions.questionTextEn:
A cache memory that has a hit rate of 0.8 has an access latency 10 ns and miss
penalty 100 ns. An optimization is done on the cache to reduce the miss rate.
However, the optimization results in an increase of cache access latency to 15 ns,
whereas the miss penalty is not affected. The minimum hit rate (rounded off to two
decimal places) needed after the optimization such that it should not increase the
average memory access time is _____________.
questions.explanationEn: Initial AMAT = 10 + (1 - 0.8)*100 = 30 ns. After optimization with hit rate h', AMAT' = 15 + (1 - h')*100 <= 30, which gives (1 - h')*100 <= 15, so 1 - h' <= 0.15 and h' >= 0.85.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the resolution of the domain name www.gate.org.in by a DNS
resolver. Assume that no resource records are cached anywhere across the DNS
servers and that iterative query mechanism is used in the resolution. The number
of DNS query-response pairs involved in completely resolving the domain name
is_____________.
questions.explanationEn: With an empty cache and iterative DNS resolution, the local resolver sends 1 query-response pair each to the Root server, the .in TLD server, the .org.in server, and finally the authoritative server for gate.org.in. Thus 4 DNS query-response pairs are required.

Consider a simple undirected unweighted graph with at least three vertices. If A is
the adjacency matrix of the graph, then the number of 3-cycles in the graph is given
by the trace of
optionsEn: 3 A

questions.explanationEn: In the adjacency matrix A of a simple undirected graph, the (i, i) diagonal entry of A^3 counts closed walks of length 3 starting and ending at vertex i. questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
optionsEn: The TLB performs an associative search in parallel on all its valid entries using page number of incoming virtual address.
If the virtual address of a word given by CPU has a TLB hit, but the subsequent search for the word results in a cache miss, then the word will always be present in the main memory.
The memory access time using a given inverted page table is always same for all incoming virtual addresses.
In a system that uses hashed page tables, if two distinct virtual addresses V1 and V2 map to the same value while hashing, then the memory access time of these addresses will not be the same.
questions.explanationEn: In an inverted page table, virtual addresses are typically looked up via hashing with chaining (or linear probing) rather than direct indexing, so collisions cause varying traversal lengths. Therefore, the claim that memory access time is always the same for all incoming virtual addresses (Option C) is false.

Consider four processes P, Q, R, and S scheduled on a CPU as per round robin
algorithm with a time quantum of 4 units. The processes arrive in the order P, Q, R,
S, all at time t = 0. There is exactly one context switch from S to Q, exactly one
context switch from R to Q, and exactly two context switches from Q to R. There is
no context switch from S to P. Switching to a ready process after the termination of
another process is also considered a context switch. Which one of the following is
NOT possible as CPU burst time (in time units) of these processes?
questions.explanationEn: With quantum q = 4 and arrival order P, Q, R, S at t = 0: P must finish in its first quantum (P <= 4) since there is no switch from S to P. For Option (D) (P=3, Q=7, R=7, S=3), the round-robin trace is P(3)->Q(4)->R(4)->S(3)->Q(3)->R(3), which has only one switch from Q to R (after S finishes, Q runs and switches to R once, then R finishes), violating the requirement of two switches from Q to R.

optionsEn: Given two Turing machines 1 2 and , M M decide if 1 2 ( ) ( ). L M L M =

questions.explanationEn: By Rice's theorem and reductions from the Halting Problem, equivalence of two TMs (A), whether L(M) is regular (B), and whether L(M) = Sigma* (C) are all undecidable. ,

G is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: The edge with the second smallest weight is always part of any minimum spanning tree of G .
One or both of the edges with the third smallest and the fourth smallest weights are part of any minimum spanning tree of G .

G can have multiple minimum spanning trees.
questions.explanationEn: Because all edge weights are distinct, G has a unique MST (so D is false). By the cut property (C), every minimum-weight edge crossing any non-trivial cut belongs to the MST. In Kruskal's algorithm, the smallest and second-smallest edges can never form a cycle, so both are in the MST (A), and among the 3rd and 4th smallest edges at most one can close a triangle with the first two, so at least one must be in the MST (B).

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

The graph has a Hamiltonian path.
The following graph is isomorphic to the Peterson graph.
The size of the largest independent set of the given graph is 3. (A subset of vertices of a graph form an independent set if no two vertices of the subset are adjacent.)
questions.explanationEn: The Petersen graph is 3-colorable (chromatic number 3, A), has a Hamiltonian path though no Hamiltonian cycle (B), and is isomorphic to the depicted 10-vertex cubic graph (C). Its maximum independent set size is 4 (not 3), making Option (D) false.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a system with 2 KB direct mapped data cache with a block size of 64 bytes.
The system has a physical address space of 64 KB and a word length of 16 bits.
During the execution of a program, four data words P, Q, R, and S are accessed in
that order 10 times (i.e., PQRSPQRS...). Hence, there are 40 accesses to data cache
altogether. Assume that the data cache is initially empty and no other data words are
accessed by the program. The addresses of the first bytes of P, Q, R, and S are
0xA248, 0xC28A, 0xCA8A, and 0xA262, respectively. For the execution of the
above program, which of the following statements is/are TRUE with respect to the
data cache?
optionsEn: Every access to S is a hit.
Once P is brought to the cache it is never evicted.
At the end of the execution only R and S reside in the cache.
Every access to R evicts Q from the cache.
questions.explanationEn: With a 2 KB direct-mapped cache and 64-byte blocks, there are 32 blocks (5 index bits, 6 offset bits, 5 tag bits). P (0xA248) and S (0xA262) share the same block (bits [15:6] are identical: 0xA240..0xA27F), so every access to S hits after P loads the block (A) and P's block at index 9 is never evicted (B). Q (0xC28A) and R (0xCA8A) map to the same index 2 with different tags, so R evicts Q on every iteration (D).

Consider a network with three routers P, Q, R shown in the figure below. All the

The routers exchange distance vector routing information and have converged on
the routing tables, after which the link Q−R fails. Assume that P and Q send out
routing updates at random times, each at the same average rate. The probability of
a routing loop formation (rounded off to one decimal place) between P and Q,
leading to count-to-infinity problem, is___________.
P

questions.explanationEn: After Q-R fails, Q knows its distance to R is infinity, while P still has distance 2 to R via Q. If P sends its update first (probability 1/2 since both send at the same average rate), Q adopts P's stale route to R with cost 3, forming a routing loop (count-to-infinity); if Q sends first, P updates to infinity and no loop forms. Hence the probability is 0.5.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a 100 Mbps link between an earth station (sender) and a satellite (receiver)
at an altitude of 2100 km. The signal propagates at a speed of 3x108 m/s. The time
taken (in milliseconds, rounded off to two decimal places) for the receiver to
completely receive a packet of 1000 bytes transmitted by the sender is_________.
questions.explanationEn: Propagation delay = (2100 * 10^3 m) / (3 * 10^8 m/s) = 7 ms. Transmission time = (1000 * 8 bits) / (100 * 10^6 bps) = 0.08 ms. Total time for the receiver to completely receive the packet = 7 + 0.08 = 7.08 ms.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the data transfer using TCP over a 1 Gbps link. Assuming that the
maximum segment lifetime (MSL) is set to 60 seconds, the minimum number of
bits required for the sequence number field of the TCP header, to prevent the
sequence number space from wrapping around during the MSL is____________.
questions.explanationEn: At 1 Gbps = 125 MB/s, over MSL = 60 s the sender can transmit 125 * 10^6 * 60 = 7.5 * 10^9 bytes. To assign unique byte sequence numbers without wrap-around, we need 2^n >= 7.5 * 10^9, which gives n = ceil(log2(7.5 * 10^9)) = 33 bits.

questions.questionTextEn:
A processor X1 operating at 2 GHz has a standard 5-stage RISC instruction pipeline
having a base CPI (cycles per instruction) of one without any pipeline hazards.
For a given program P that has 30% branch instructions, control hazards incur 2
cycles stall for every branch. A new version of the processor X2 operating at same
clock frequency has an additional branch predictor unit (BPU) that completely
eliminates stalls for correctly predicted branches. There is neither any savings nor
any additional stalls for wrong predictions. There are no structural hazards and data
hazards for X1 and X2. If the BPU has a prediction accuracy of 80%, the speed up
(rounded off to two decimal places) obtained by X2 over X1 in executing
P is____________.
questions.explanationEn: For X1, CPI = 1 + 0.30 * 2 = 1.60. For X2, only the 20% mispredicted branches incur the 2-cycle stall, so CPI_2 = 1 + 0.30 * 0.20 * 2 = 1.12. Since clock frequency is unchanged, speedup = 1.60 / 1.12 = 1.4286 (in range 1.42 to 1.45).
